rounds.text: Gravity (India) Ltd is exceptionally under-appreciated by the market, trading at a low P/E of 5.24x against a sector benchmark of 16.4x [E1, E6]. This low multiple stands in stark contrast to phenomenal recent expansion, demonstrated by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 160% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 1568% [E16, E21]. Operational profitability is elite, featuring an astronomical ROCE of 100.5% compared to a sector benchmark of 7.7%, alongside an ROE of 86.17% [E8, E10]. Furthermore, the business is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13x and shrinking borrowings [E38, E39]. Fundamentals are drastically outpacing price performance, with a reverse DCF revealing that the current price implies a negative 11.2% earnings growth against the 18.0% base case assumption [E45, E46]. Conceded: promoter holding has fallen to 6.05% and cash conversion against reported profit was weak for Mar 2026 [E34, E41].

The most concerning aspect of Gravity (India) Ltd is the disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation, as evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 0.00x for March 2026 [E34]. Despite reporting profits, the company generated Rs 0 Cr in operating and free cash flow during that period [E35, E36], suggesting that earnings are heavily reliant on receivables or accruals rather than realized cash [E34]. This lack of liquidity is compounded by a significant decline in promoter confidence, with holdings dropping from 24.21% to just 6.05% over the last three years [E41, E53]. Furthermore, the company’s operating margin has shown volatility, contracting by 32 percentage points in the June 2026 quarter compared to the previous year [E31]. While the stock trades at a high price-to-book ratio of 6.60x [E2, E51], the lack of any dividend yield provides no income buffer for investors [E4]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent growth in sales and profits [E17, E21, E55, E57] and maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio [E38].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.00x and operating cash flow was Rs 0 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. However, this reported cash figure exists alongside exceptional fundamental delivery, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 138% and profit growth of 115% [E15, E19]. The bear points to promoter selling [E41, E53], but completely ignores that fundamentals are vastly outpacing the share price, with profit growth outpacing 5-year price growth and a recent 1-year performance where profit growth exceeded share price growth by 1434% [E46, E47]. On valuation and return metrics, the bear objects to the price-to-book ratio [E2, E51], yet the company boasts a sector-crushing ROA of 46.52% and an ROCE of 100.5% against sector benchmarks of 2.49% and 7.7% respectively [E8, E10]. Furthermore, the bear highlights margin volatility in a single quarter [E31], but overlooks that the yearly operating-margin trend has been increasing over the last 4 years [E32] and that the business remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13x [E38]. Finally, while the bear cites a zero dividend yield [E4], this reflects a growth-oriented business whose intrinsic value via a discounted cash flow leaves a massive margin of safety [E43, E44], with current pricing implying negative earnings growth against the base case [E45].

Conceded: five-year compounded sales growth reached 138% and profit growth reached 115% [E15, E19]. Despite these reported metrics, the bull's emphasis on fundamental outperformance ignores the alarming reality that operating and free cash flow for March 2026 stood at precisely Rs 0 Cr, yielding a 0.00x cash conversion ratio where profits bear no relation to actual cash collected [E34, E35, E36]. Conceded: the yearly operating-margin trend is marked as increasing over the last four years [E32]. However, this historical comfort is directly undermined by the most recent quarterly data showing operating margins crashing by 32 percentage points down to 13% in June 2026 compared to the prior year [E31], alongside an inconsistent quarterly trend [E33]. While the bull dismisses promoter reduction as irrelevant against return metrics, promoter ownership has collapsed to a negligible 6.05% following an 18.16 percentage point drop since September 2023 [E41, E52, E53]. Finally, pointing to a discounted cash flow margin of safety ignores that the stock trades at 6.60x book value [E2, E44, E51] and pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], leaving outside shareholders bearing all the risk of uncollected profits with almost zero insider skin in the game.

Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.00x for March 2026 with operating and free cash flows at Rs 0 Cr [E34, E35, E36], but this must be balanced against a conservatively financed balance sheet where borrowings decreased to Rs 2 Cr and debt-to-equity is just 0.13x [E38, E39]. Conceded: operating margins dropped 32 percentage points in June 2026 [E31] and promoter holdings declined to 6.05% [E41], yet the yearly operating-margin trend has successfully expanded over the last four years [E32], and fundamentals continue to dramatically outpace the stock's price history [E46, E47]. The bear's concern over a 6.60x price-to-book ratio [E2] ignores the overwhelming fundamental reality of an exceptional 100.5% to 159.0% ROCE and an 86.17% to 151.0% ROE [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13] that dwarf sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. Furthermore, pointing to a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] overlooks the company's staggering 5-year sales growth of 138% and profit growth of 115% [E15, E19], which demonstrate that capital is being deployed to fuel explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion rather than being idly distributed.

Conceded: borrowings are down to Rs 2 Cr with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.13x [E38, E39], but the claim that capital is deployed to fuel expansion ignores the stark reality of Rs 0 Cr in operating and free cash flow alongside a 0.00x cash conversion ratio for March 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. The assertion that yearly operating margins have expanded over four years [E32] glosses over the severe 32 percentage point drop in the June 2026 quarterly operating margin and an inconsistent short-term trend [E31, E33]. While the bull dismisses the 6.60x price-to-book valuation [E2] by highlighting extraordinary ROE and ROCE figures [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13], those stellar returns must be heavily discounted against a 10-year median ROE of just 1% [E26] and a 5-year median ROE of 9% [E27]. Furthermore, pointing to explosive multi-year sales and profit growth [E15, E19] fails to justify a complete absence of dividend distributions [E4] when promoters continue to aggressively exit the business, slashing their holdings down to a negligible 6.05% [E41]. Conceded: fundamentals have outpaced past price action [E46, E47], yet that dynamic offers little comfort to minority shareholders facing massive insider abandonment and zero cash realization from reported earnings [E34, E35, E41].
